Contingent fees support lean research teams, but estate delays defer cash.; economics: gross revenue range: $80,000–$600,000 USD annually; net profit margin range: 25–50%; owner net profit potential: $20,000–$300,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $10,000–$50,000 USD; monthly opex range: $2,000–$10,000 USD; time to first deal: 6–24 months; typical team size: full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Recognized service fees, not client asset value; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data; scenarios: conservative: annual gross revenue usd: 80000; net profit margin pct: 25; annual owner net profit usd: 20000; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; base case: annual gross revenue usd: 340000.0; net profit margin pct: 37.5; annual owner net profit usd: 127500; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; scaled small team: annual gross revenue usd: 600000; net profit margin pct: 50; annual owner net profit usd: 300000; full time including owner: 2; contractors: 4; total people: 6; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Public-record alerts; Genealogy case tracking; Document indexing; key risks: Unsuccessful research; Contested kinship; Long collection cycles; regulatory notes: Check heir-finder fee restrictions and solicitation rules by jurisdiction.; Do not provide legal representation without appropriate authorization.; track ids: track_1; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; plays: id: public_record_api_intelligence; track id: track_1; name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.; inputs: Court & probate dockets; State controller ledgers; Public licensing & entity APIs; workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence; Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold; Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution; metrics: Cost per verified lead; Docket-to-contact latency (hours); Net recovery / conversion rate; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; id: unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery; mechanism: Ingest state controller/treasury escheatment ledgers and uncashed municipal/corporate warrant registries above $25,000, cross-match corporate officers via Secretary of State filings, and execute statutory recovery agreements for a 10–25% contingent finder fee.; inputs: State controller/treasury escheatment bulk ledgers; Uncashed municipal warrant & vendor-credit registries; Secretary of State officer & FEIN cross-match index; workflow: Filter state unclaimed-property and uncashed-warrant ledgers for high-value corporate and estate accounts exceeding $25,000; Resolve active corporate officers, successor entities, or authorized fiduciaries via SOS and skip-trace databases; Execute state-compliant finder agreements with statutory fee caps and submit notarized claim packages to the treasury administrator; metrics: Average gross warrant/escheatment claim size ($25k+); Treasury claim approval rate (%); Days from notarized filing to state disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory finder-fee cap violation or waiting-period rejection; trigger: Charging above state statutory fee limits (e.g., 10% in CA/FL/NY) or soliciting claims during restricted post-escheatment windows; impact: Voided recovery contract, state controller rejection, or administrative penalty; detection metric: State-by-state fee-cap compliance check (100% pass) and claim rejection notice rate; fallback: Enforce per-state statutory fee caps and waiting-period rules in intake templates and disclose the owner's right to claim directly for free; id: probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping; mechanism: Parse county probate petitions (Letters Testamentary / Letters of Administration) and daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) filings before national aggregators index them, matching out-of-state personal representatives and distressed owners to licensed probate brokers and cash buyers.; inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings; County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds; Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline; workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing; Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records; Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions; metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days); Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%); Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting; trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits; impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement; detection metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges; fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record; id: forced_pooling_mineral_lease_curve_jumping; track id: track_1; name: Forced-Pooling Docket & Non-Consent Mineral Lease Curve-Jumping Arbitrage; mechanism: Use public pooling applications and drilling schedules to identify unleased mineral interests before election deadlines, pricing royalty upside against title defects and non-consent cost exposure.; inputs: State pooling dockets and election orders; Mineral ownership chain and lease abstracts; Operator development plans and local lease comparables; workflow: 1. Monitor pooling applications and map affected mineral tracts and hearing dates; 2. Verify net mineral acres, ownership authority, and election consequences with specialist counsel; 3. Negotiate disclosed lease or option terms and fund obligations before applicable deadlines; 4. Assign permitted interests or administer royalty receipts with division-order reconciliation; metrics: Verified net mineral acres acquired; Election deadlines met (%); Net royalty or assignment proceeds per invested dollar; platform risks: failure mode: Missed election or unexpected non-consent penalty; trigger: Stale docket feed or misread state-specific pooling order; impact: Delayed royalties and unbudgeted development-cost exposure; detection metric: Unverified order changes and days remaining to election; fallback: Stop acquisitions pending counsel review and choose only timely, fully understood permitted elections; id: fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing; track id: track_1; name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing; mechanism: Acquire documented fractional heir interests at a discount reflecting illiquidity, then seek consensual buyouts or counsel-supervised partition subject to heirs-property protections and co-owner rights.; inputs: Probate files and verified heirship records; Title chain, occupancy facts, and independent appraisal; Applicable partition and heirs-property protection rules; workflow: 1. Establish ownership fractions, probate authority, and encumbrances before contacting sellers; 2. Provide transparent offers with independent-advice opportunity and modeled partition costs; 3. Seek voluntary co-owner buyouts or an agreed market sale before considering litigation; 4. If unresolved, use counsel-led statutory procedures honoring notice, appraisal, and buyout rights; metrics: Verified ownership share acquired; Consensual resolution rate; Net proceeds after carrying and legal costs; platform risks: failure mode: Heirs-property protections defeat assumed forced-sale economics; trigger: Mandatory co-owner buyout, partition-in-kind preference, or defective heirship; impact: Long holding period and lower realizable value; detection metric: Unresolved heirs and statutory buyout conditions per property; fallback: Renegotiate voluntary exits or retain the interest without threatening unavailable remedies; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; play id: public_record_api_intelligence; play name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; track id: track_1; failure mode: Statutory finder-fee cap violation or waiting-period rejection; trigger: Charging above state statutory fee limits (e.g., 10% in CA/FL/NY) or soliciting claims during restricted post-escheatment windows; impact: Voided recovery contract, state controller rejection, or administrative penalty; detection metric: State-by-state fee-cap compliance check (100% pass) and claim rejection notice rate; fallback: Enforce per-state statutory fee caps and waiting-period rules in intake templates and disclose the owner's right to claim directly for free; play id: unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage; play name: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery; track id: track_1; failure mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting; trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits; impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement; detection metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges; fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record; play id: probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage; play name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping; track id: track_1; failure mode: Missed election or unexpected non-consent penalty; trigger: Stale docket feed or misread state-specific pooling order; impact: Delayed royalties and unbudgeted development-cost exposure; detection metric: Unverified order changes and days remaining to election; fallback: Stop acquisitions pending counsel review and choose only timely, fully understood permitted elections; play id: forced_pooling_mineral_lease_curve_jumping; play name: Forced-Pooling Docket & Non-Consent Mineral Lease Curve-Jumping Arbitrage; track id: track_1; failure mode: Heirs-property protections defeat assumed forced-sale economics; trigger: Mandatory co-owner buyout, partition-in-kind preference, or defective heirship; impact: Long holding period and lower realizable value; detection metric: Unresolved heirs and statutory buyout conditions per property; fallback: Renegotiate voluntary exits or retain the interest without threatening unavailable remedies; play id: fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing; play name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing; track id: track_1
